_readme: All simulated AI output and app copy for the Admit Pal prototype lives in this file. Edit freely. School numbers are illustrative mock data, not official class profiles. Text supports {placeholders}: name, school, short, gmat, median, gmatDiff, gpa, gpaMedian, years, weMedian, industry, n, count. Plan, assistant and advisor text also supports: date, k, wordCount, minutes, essayPrompt, leadStory, assistant. Deadlines and essay prompts are illustrative mock data. Each school's requirements (recommenders, essays, extras), tuition and focus areas are illustrative mock data too. Advice text also supports: focus, focusWanted, tuition, budget, industryFrom.

plan._note: Action plan. Each school's items come from its own requirements (schools[].requirements): the recommenders row uses its count, the essay row repeats once per essay (staggered by stagger_days), and each entry in extras adds the matching row from plan.extras. Each date is the school's deadline minus days_before. 'assistant' picks which assistant opens. only_if: gmat_missing or gmat_below. status_updates says what happens to the plan when a status is saved in the outcome nudge.

assistants._note: Assistant workspaces opened from plan items. Each assistant answers with the first reply whose keyword appears in the user's message, otherwise default_reply. There is no typing box: documents are uploaded so each one is captured with its school and plan item (the data loop). requires_upload means the item can't be completed or sent for expert review without a document. The Essay Coach is live when the page is served by essay_server.py with an API key: replies come from the model picked in the workspace (Anthropic, OpenAI, DeepSeek or Gemini, see live below) and the keyword replies are the offline fallback.

essay.name: Essay Coach
essay.intro: Hi {name}! Let's work on your {short} essay. The prompt is: "{essayPrompt}" Upload a draft above and ask me for feedback, or ask me how to get started.

replies.reply: Start with a short outline: (1) a moment from your work that showed you the problem, (2) why this field, (3) the specific role you want after the MBA, (4) two or three {short} resources that close the gap. Aim for one paragraph each.

I read your {wordCount}-word draft. What works: you show clear impact. To improve: (1) your first paragraph is about the company, not you; open with your own decision. (2) Name a specific post-MBA role. (3) Mention one {short} course or club by name.
Your draft is {wordCount} words. This one has a {wordLimit}-word limit, so trim or expand toward it.
Don't use the main essay to explain your score. If you need to address it, use the optional essay in two or three plain sentences.

essay.default_reply: Good question. For {short}, keep returning to your lead story: {leadStory} Want feedback on your draft? Type 'review my draft'.

recommender.name: Recommender Advisor
recommender.intro: Hi {name}, I'll help you choose recommenders for {short}. Upload your notes on the people you're considering, or ask me who to pick.

replies.reply: Pick your current direct manager and a senior colleague from your biggest project. Both can speak to your leadership with specific examples. Avoid a senior name who barely knows your work.
Send each recommender a one-page brief: your goals, why {short}, and three stories you'd like them to mention. Ask at least six weeks before the deadline.
From your notes, your manager is the strongest choice. Make sure the second recommender has seen you lead, not just analyze.

recommender.default_reply: Recommenders should know your work well and be able to give specific examples. Ask me 'who should I pick?' or 'how do I brief them?'.

test_prep.name: GMAT Coach
test_prep.intro: Hi {name}, {short}'s median GMAT is {median}. Want a study plan to get there?

replies.reply: Six-week plan: weeks 1-2 on Quant fundamentals (1 hour a day), weeks 3-4 on Data Insights, then a full practice test every Saturday in weeks 5-6. Book your test date now so you have time for a retake.
Focus on rates, ratios and number properties first; they account for most missed Quant questions.
Do two timed reading comprehension passages a day and review every wrong answer.

test_prep.default_reply: I can build a study plan, focus on Quant or Verbal, or help you pick a test date. What would help?

interview.name: Interview Coach
interview.intro: Congratulations on the {short} interview, {name}! Let's prepare. Type 'mock' to start a practice question, or upload an answer above for feedback.

replies.reply: Practice question: "Walk me through your resume." Keep it to two minutes: where you started, the two promotions, why this path, and why an MBA now.
Your answer is {wordCount} words, about {minutes} minutes spoken. Good structure. Cut the first job to one sentence and spend more time on why {short}.
For 'Why {short}?', name two specific things (a class, a club, a professor) and connect each to your goal.

interview.default_reply: I can run a mock question, review an answer, or help you prepare 'Why {short}?'. Type 'mock' to start.
